subject: Launch bandwidth alignment & temporary rate carveout for HeroHealth pilot
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Launch bandwidth alignment & tempo carveout request — HeroHealth pilot

Team,

Quick one: HeroHealth confirmed their pilot launch window for the week of Apr 8. Sam says early-day traffic could spike as they run a targeted onboarding campaign (SMS + in-app). They expect a burst to ~18 QPS for ~45 minutes during initial onboarding, then a sustained 3–4 QPS for the first two days.

As this is a pilot tied to an enterprise POC (deal D-43821), Sam is asking for a short-term uplift in entitlement and a temporary rate carveout to avoid early throttling while they warm up caching.

Asks:
- Product: can we safely allow a temporary per-customer burst to 20 QPS for a 2-hour window with automatic rollback? (Kimberly)
- Capacity/Quota: what level of dedicated headroom do we need to reserve and how will it affect other pilots? (Marissa)
- Sales/CS: confirm timing and can we capture a scoped MA plan in HubSpot that matches the window? (Karthik)

Attachments: I uploaded Sam's traffic projection (herohealth_traffic_projection.xlsx).

If we can get a short yes/no by EOD, I’ll coordinate with Sam and procurement to lock dates.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 11:19:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch bandwidth alignment & tempo carveout request — HeroHealth pilot

Ben — thanks for the context and the projection. Quick notes from product:

- Short-term temporary burst to 20 QPS is feasible if we limit it to a single customer token and gate by time window + request fingerprinting.
- We need an explicit rollback policy: auto-revert after 2 hours and a manual kill switch if latency > 600ms or error rate > 1.5%.
- PM asks for a short alpha config: model variant pinned to gpt-compat-small for the burst and fallback to gpt-compat-medium if errors occur. That minimizes memory pressure.

Can Marissa confirm whether we have that headroom without impacting the scheduled Dedicated customers?

-Kim
Kimberly Park | Head of Product, Serving
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch bandwidth alignment & tempo carveout request — HeroHealth pilot

Folks — ran a quick capacity sweep with infra. TL;DR: we can cover a single 2-hour 20 QPS spike if we provision a transient soft-reservation on one shared pool and schedule soft-bursting rules. Details:

- Impact: ~12% transient throughput headroom taken from the general burst pool for that window. Marginal CPU and memory overhead minimal if Kimberly's fallback rules are used.
- Risk: if another customer triggers a simultaneous burst, we'll fallback anyone on gpt-compat-small to queued short-latency mode.
- Ops ask: need written approval from Sales + a signed MA plan clause that this is a one-time, non-recurring carveout (Procurement signoff helps).

I attached the runbook snippet and the proposed entitlement amendment (proposed_entitlement_amendment.pdf). I can schedule the provisioning for Apr 7 02:00–04:00 UTC to test before their Apr 8 ramp.

-Marissa
Senior Program Manager, Capacity Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Sam Hart <sam.hart@herohealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch bandwidth alignment & tempo carveout request — HeroHealth pilot

Ben, thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

We can confirm the pilot marketing push will start Apr 8 10:00 AM ET. The most painful risk for us is early throttling in the first 30–60 minutes as our onboarding flow fires verification prompts to new users. The attached projections are conservative.

We are happy to sign a one-off amendment to cover the burst window; procurement is looped (procurement@herohealth.com). Two asks from our side:
1) Can you provide a rollback SLA in writing (we need assurance we'll be able to cancel the carveout if unexpected behavior occurs)?
2) Can Redwood provide a short post-mortem if anything causes increased latency for other customers?

If you schedule the Apr 7 test window that works for us.

—Sam
Sam Hart | Head of Engineering, HeroHealth
